title: A monopoly from a key resource: price, profit, deadweight loss, elasticity and a per-unit tax
scenario: Corvane Labs (invented) owns the only supply of a rare reagent that home test kits for water quality need, so no other firm can make the kits and Corvane is the only seller. It maximizes profit and is earning a positive economic profit. Its marginal cost curve is U-shaped and passes through the minimum of its average total cost curve.

stimulus.title: Corvane Labs at its profit-maximizing output
stimulus.html:
Corvane Labs, per week, at the output where MR = MC (invented data for practice)
MeasureValue
Quantity of kits200
Price per kit (dollars)40
Average total cost per kit (dollars)25
Marginal revenue and marginal cost (dollars)18

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled graph for Corvane Labs showing demand, marginal revenue, marginal cost and average total cost, and show its profit-maximizing price and quantity, labeled PM and QM.

rubric.point: A correctly labeled graph: axes "Price and cost" and "Quantity", a downward-sloping D, MR below D, and MC crossing ATC at the minimum of ATC.
accept: MR drawn below demand and steeper

rubric.point: QM where MR = MC, with PM read from the demand curve above QM, both marked on the axes.
accept: dotted lines from the point on demand to both axes

parts.sample: Price and cost on the vertical axis, Quantity on the horizontal. D slopes down; MR starts at the same point on the price axis and lies below D; MC is U-shaped and crosses ATC at the lowest point of ATC. QM is where MR crosses MC; going straight up from QM to D gives PM. ATC at QM lies below PM, so the firm earns a profit.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Shade the area of Corvane Labs' economic profit.

rubric.point: Shades the rectangle between PM and ATC at QM, from zero to QM, completely.
accept: (PM - ATC) x QM shown as a rectangle

parts.sample: Economic profit is the rectangle from PM down to ATC at QM, and from the vertical axis out to QM.

slips.tr: That is total revenue. Profit is only the part between PM and ATC.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Shade the deadweight loss caused by the monopoly.

rubric.point: Shades the area between demand and MC, from QM to the quantity where demand meets MC.
accept: the triangle between D and MC to the right of QM

parts.sample: The deadweight loss is the triangle between the demand curve and the MC curve, from QM out to the quantity where demand crosses MC. It is not shaded down to ATC.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Calculate Corvane Labs' weekly economic profit using the data in the table. Show your work.

rubric.point: Profit of $3,000 with work shown: (40 minus 25) times 200, or 8,000 minus 5,000.

parts.sample: Profit = (P minus ATC) times Q = ($40 minus $25) times 200 = $15 times 200 = $3,000 a week.

parts.label: E(i)
parts.prompt: Identify whether demand for the kits is elastic, inelastic or unit elastic at QM.

parts.label: E(ii)

rubric.point: Explains that marginal revenue at QM is positive (MR = MC = $18 > 0), and MR is positive only on the elastic part of demand (a lower price would raise total revenue).
accept: MR > 0 so total revenue rises as price falls, so demand is elastic
the monopolist produces above the unit-elastic point where MR = 0

parts.sample: At QM, MR equals MC, which is $18, so MR is positive. Marginal revenue is positive only on the elastic part of the demand curve, where a lower price raises total revenue; it is zero at the unit-elastic point. So demand is elastic at QM.

parts.label: F(i)
parts.prompt: The government places a per-unit tax of $5 on each kit Corvane Labs sells. Show the effect of the tax on your graph in part A by shifting the curve or curves that change.

rubric.point: MC shifts up (and ATC with it); demand and MR do not move
accept: MC2 above MC1, D and MR unchanged

parts.sample: A tax on each kit adds $5 to the cost of every extra kit, so MC shifts up to MC2, and ATC shifts up with it. Demand and MR do not move.

key.because: a per-unit tax on each kit, a variable cost

slips.D: The tax is paid by the seller on each unit; buyers' willingness to pay, and so demand, does not change.
slips.ATC: A per-unit tax adds to the cost of every extra kit, so MC moves up (and ATC with it).

parts.label: F(ii)
parts.prompt: Identify what happens to the quantity of kits Corvane Labs sells and to the price it charges after the tax, compared with QM and PM.

rubric.point: The quantity decreases and the price increases

parts.sample: The quantity falls, because the higher MC now crosses MR at a smaller quantity, and the price rises, because a smaller quantity is read at a higher point on the demand curve.

parts.label: F(iii)
parts.prompt: Identify what happens to the deadweight loss in the market for kits after the tax, and explain.

rubric.point: The deadweight loss increases, because the quantity sold moves further below the allocatively efficient quantity, where demand meets the original MC
accept: it increases: output falls further below the efficient quantity

parts.sample: The deadweight loss increases. Before the tax Corvane already sold fewer kits than the efficient quantity, where demand meets the original MC (the true cost of making a kit). The tax cuts output further, so even more kits that buyers value above their cost of production are not made.
